speaker: Narrator
text: The tent is quieter now — not because the fighting has stopped

speaker: Narrator
text: but because many inside no longer have the strength to respond to it.

speaker: Narrator
text: By early April 1942, Bataan had been under siege for nearly three months.

speaker: Narrator
text: No reinforcements had arrived.

speaker: Narrator
text: No resupply had broken through the blockade.

speaker: Narrator
text: Ammunition was critically low, forcing units to conserve fire or abandon positions altogether.

speaker: Narrator
text: Entire regiments had been reduced to fractions of their original strength.

speaker: Narrator
text: Some soldiers could no longer stand without support.

speaker: Narrator
text: Others remained in line despite fever, ordered to hold positions that could no longer be defended.

speaker: Narrator
text: For months, they had held on with the expectation that help might come.

speaker: Narrator
text: But by now, that hope had begun to fade.

speaker: Narrator
text: Command was no longer deciding how to win the battle—

speaker: Narrator
text: but whether to continue holding on…

speaker: Narrator
text: or to prevent what remained of the force from being completely destroyed.

speaker: Narrator
text: From inside the command tent, the outside world is reduced to fragments—

speaker: Narrator
text: a partially opened canvas flap,

speaker: Narrator
text: a narrow strip of fading daylight,

speaker: Narrator
text: and the faint, irregular sound of water falling from a nearly empty canteen.

speaker: General King
text: I can hear it… even over everything else.

speaker: General King
text: The silence between suffering.

speaker: Narrator
text: A soldier lies near the edge of the tent.

speaker: Narrator
text: His uniform hangs loose, no longer fitting a body that has been stripped down by hunger and exhaustion.

speaker: Narrator
text: Beside him, a canteen hangs at an angle—its last drops falling slowly into nothing.

speaker: Narrator
text: Each drop echoes louder than gunfire.

speaker: General King
text: Even water... is rationed down to time.

speaker: Narrator
text: Food stocks meant for months had been consumed in weeks after the retreat into Bataan.

speaker: Narrator
text: Pack animals had long since been slaughtered for meat.

speaker: Narrator
text: What remained was stretched beyond its limit.

speaker: Narrator
text: What remained was stretched beyond its limit.

speaker: Narrator
text: Many had been fighting without proper rest for weeks—

speaker: Narrator
text: rotating between the front lines and overcrowded aid stations,

speaker: Narrator
text: only to return again with less strength than before.

speaker: Narrator
text: Outside this tent, more than 70,000 American and Filipino troops remained on the peninsula—

speaker: Narrator
text: most of them weakened, many unable to fight,

speaker: Narrator
text: all waiting for orders that would decide what happened next.

speaker: Narrator
text: They had been told to hold.

speaker: Narrator
text: And they had.

speaker: Narrator
text: But time—

speaker: Narrator
text: and strength—

speaker: Narrator
text: were no longer on their side.
